highlights.text: ṭāʾ and lām point to three root meanings: the tender freshness of a thing, overlooking (al-ishrāf), and nullifying something
al-ṭall is the weakest kind of rain
a single sound root meaning excess and extension in a thing
طَالَ … يَطُولُ طُولًا = "to be long/tall."
طَاوَلْتُهُ فَطُلْتُهُ = "I vied in height with him and outmatched him"
Ṭarafa likens death (as long as it spares a youth) to a slackened tether whose folds are still held in the hand
one stable root meaning the inner/intimate side of a thing, the side that faces inward
الْبَطْن (the belly) is the opposite of الظَّهْر (the back)
بَاطِنُ الْأَمْر is a matter's hidden interior, as opposed to its ظاهر (outward face)
بِطَانَة — a man's close confidants who know his private affairs
one core idea: separating or cutting a thing off from something else (ibānah)
glossing it simply as "cut yourself off to Him, a complete cutting-off"
two roots: one of lowness and flatness, and one of pounding
The entry cites Q 18:98, "He will make it level (dakkāʾ)"
Dakaktu l-shayʾ, "I pounded the thing", equivalent to daqaqtuhu
the root signals something departing/moving away from something else, and — he stresses — always gently, not violently
"Dalakati ash-shamsu" (the sun dalakat) — the sun declined [past its zenith]
a single root meaning an opening-up or bursting-open in something
Dawn (al-fajr): the darkness "bursting open" to let the morning through
Water bursting forth (infajara al-māʾ): water breaking open and flowing out
Ibn Fāris cites Labīd, using fājir of a part of a mount that "leans/deviates" aside
reliance on someone else in a matter -- handing a matter over to another and referring it to him
"he entrusted/delegated his affair to him," i.e. he referred it to that person
"wa-ufawwidu amri ila Llah" -- "and I commit my affair to Allah" (Ghafir 40:44)
a single root with one consistent analogy: a thing being uncovered
تَجَلَّى الشَّيْءُ — a thing becomes manifest, i.e. is uncovered
جَلَا الْقَوْمُ عَنْ مَنَازِلِهِمْ (jalāʾ) — a people quit their dwellings
when he drove them out with smoke (the bees), they scattered in groups
a single, consistent root — something going forward headlong, overpowering restraint by sheer force
has overpowered its rider and bolted out of control
the sense given is yasʿawna, "they run/rush [toward it]"
"I cast off my rein, headlong — no rebuke turns me back from fair women like statues"
two distinct base senses: (1) gathering-together and largeness of build, and (2) beauty
"as a single whole" (jumlatan wāḥidatan)
الْجَمَال = beauty, the opposite of ugliness
"Restrain yourself, O wounded heart — you shall meet the one you love and find rest."
a single sound root whose core sense is the departure of strength or vigor from a thing
الْمَوْت (al-mawt) — death, the opposite of life
an animal (of a normally edible kind) that has died
Buy of the inert property (mawatān), not of the living stock (ḥayawān)
highlights.note: saying of the Arabs, via al-Aṣmaʿī

highlights.text: Ibn Fāris grounds his "departure of strength" reading in a Prophetic saying about the pungent plant (garlic/onion)
one physical image: something liquid being agitated/churned inside the container that holds it
the term for a pregnant female overtaken by labor pains (al-ṭalq)
two distinct roots — one for strength, one for emptiness/barrenness
القُوَّة (quwwa) = strength; القَوِيّ = the strong, opposite of the weak
المُقْوِي (in this sense) = a man carrying no provisions
one core idea: the fixedness or permanence of a thing that is held or retained, whether by legal right or otherwise
al-rahn — "the pledge": a thing given/held as security
**Fixing/driving something into something else so it goes downward**
**A sound.**
Three distinct roots: (1) a disease, (2) a color, (3) a kind of running.
al-ramād — ash (the well-known substance)
a proverb about ruining one's own good work at the last moment ("your brother roasted it, then buried it in ash")
a single core idea: spreading and extending something flat
two distinct roots: one denoting a kind of worship, the other a kind of physical exertion
التَّسْبِيح (al-tasbīḥ): declaring God to be far removed (tanzīh)
سُبْحَانَ مِنْ كَذَا, meaning "how far removed / how astonishing is such-and-such."
Shāhid: a line of al-Aʿshā using subḥāna of the boaster ʿAlqama
He cites the jurists' usage: a traveler joins two prayers and does not "tusabbiḥ" between them
from a ḥadīth, meaning God's majesty and greatness
by his account it denotes filling in a thing and making it fit close
Every barrier between two things is called a sadd
al-sadīd is one who has sadād, straightness
"They let me go to waste, and what a young man they wasted, for a day of dire trouble and for stopping a frontier gap."
one root whose core idea is colour that is *not* white — darkness or dusk of hue
i.e. those who "samurūn" (converse in the dark)
"wa-sāmirin ṭāla lahum fīhi al-samar" — "and many a night-gathering in which their talk ran long."
the idiom "lā ātīka al-samar wa-l-qamar"
a single, regular root meaning: completeness or perfection
tamma al-shayʾ means the thing became complete; atmamtuhu means "I completed it"
Al-Nābigha boasts: "I give my partners at the arrows their full share, grant them favours twice over, and cover the great bowl with fat."
corruption or derangement of the bodily limbs/faculties
al-khabal = insanity
a verse of the poet Aws, who describes a hand as makhbūlah ("maimed") in its upper arm
found in ḥadīth, is said [by others — Ibn Fāris reports the claim, not as his own assertion] to mean the pus/discharge of the people of the Fire
two separate origins: (1) knowledge, and (2) softness, looseness, and abundance
خُبْر (khubr) is knowledge or acquaintance with something
The divine name الخَبِير (al-Khabīr) means the one who knows everything
The forbidden مُخَابَرَة (mukhābara) is sharecropping for a half, third, or other share of the crop
خَزِيَ (khaziya) as denoting a "breaking" or abasement that overtakes a person
This is the sense in the Qurʾānic uses of khizy, e.g. "that is for them a disgrace in this world" (Q 5:33)
is closer to al-khizy (abasement from another)
